The test image shows a seedling emerging from dark, wet soil — it appears collapsed and brown at the soil line with rotted tissue. This points to a damping-off or early seedling disease. Top candidates: **Pythium_damping_off**, **Rhizoctonia**, **Phytophthora**.

Let me view reference images for these candidates simultaneously.
The test image shows a brown, collapsed seedling at the soil line on wet, dark soil. Let me also check Fusarium for comparison.
I've viewed 6 reference images so far. Need at least 12. Let me check more candidates to be thorough.

Now I have 12 reference images viewed. Let me analyze the evidence:

**Test image observations:**
- Very early seedling stage, just barely emerging from soil
- Brown/tan collapsed tissue at soil level — the entire emerging seedling is browned and soft-looking
- Surrounding soil is dark, wet, and moist
- No green tissue visible — seedling has died/rotted before or at emergence
- Soft, non-firm appearance (no distinct red-brown dry lesion)

**Comparison to candidates:**
- **Pythium_damping_off**: Reference shows very small just-emerged seedlings on wet dark soil with collapsed/rotted tissue — nearly identical scene (wet soil, early stage, rotted seedling). Best match.
- **Rhizoctonia**: Distinctive reddish-brown, firm, dry lesions on hypocotyl at soil line. The test image tissue appears soft and uniformly brown, not the crisp reddish lesion of Rhizoctonia.
- **Phytophthora**: Dark brown lesion extending up from taproot on more developed seedlings/plants. Not matching this very early pre/post-emergence rot stage.
- All other candidates involve leaf lesions, stem cankers, or mature plant symptoms — not applicable here.

The combination of **wet dark soil**, **pre/post-emergence seedling collapse**, and **soft brown rotted tissue** at emergence is the hallmark presentation of Pythium damping off.
